items.title: Section: A Single Coin Refused — What Severed Affliction Actually Looks Like

items.zh: 復次，煩惱斷已，於可愛法若劣、若勝、若現在前、若不現前，雖猛利見而觀察之，亦不染著。如於可愛而不生愛，如是於可瞋法亦不生瞋，於可癡法亦不生癡。又眼見諸色，不喜不憂，但住於捨，正念正知。如眼見色，乃至意知法亦爾。又性少欲，成就第一真實少欲。如少欲，如是喜足、遠離、勇猛精進、安住正念、寂定、聰慧亦爾。於無戲論任性好樂，於有戲論策勵其心方能緣慮。如是等輩，當知煩惱已斷之相。
items.en: Moreover, once affliction has been severed, with respect to agreeable dharmas, whether inferior or superior, present or not present, though examined closely with forceful attention, no attachment arises. Just as with the agreeable, so too with what might provoke anger, no anger arises, and with what might provoke confusion, no confusion arises. And seeing forms with the eye, one is neither joyful nor sorrowful, but abides in equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending. As with seeing forms, so too through cognizing mental objects with the mind. One is by nature of few desires, accomplishing the foremost, genuine fewness of desire. As with fewness of desire, so too with contentment, seclusion, vigorous diligence, abiding in mindfulness, settled stability, and wisdom. One naturally delights in what is free of conceptual proliferation, and must rouse the mind with effort to engage what involves it. Such as these should be known as the marks of affliction already severed.

items.title: Section: Eight Questions Closed — Security, Coolness, and a Task Complete

items.zh: 復次，煩惱斷者有多勝利。謂隨證得超越憂、苦，超越喜、樂，超越色想及與有對種種性想，超惡趣苦，超越生等一切種苦。又證安隱第一安隱。又證清涼第一清涼。又得第一現法樂住，隨其自心自在而轉。若行、若住，隨所欲樂所證之法無復退轉。於自義利圓滿究竟，於諸所作無復希望。
items.en: Moreover, one who has severed affliction has many benefits. According to attainment, one transcends distress and pain, transcends joy and pleasure, transcends the perception of form and every perception of sense-based resistance, transcends the suffering of the evil destinies, and transcends every kind of suffering belonging to birth and the rest. One also attains security, the foremost security. One also attains coolness, the foremost coolness. One also attains the foremost present-life joyful abiding, turning freely according to one's own mind. Whether walking or standing, whatever is attained according to one's own wish no longer regresses. One's own good is fulfilled to its very completion, with nothing further left to be done.

items.title: Section: Benefiting Every Being, and Fifteen Objects Affliction References

items.zh: 或復有一修利他行，為欲利益安樂眾生，哀愍世間，令諸天人利益安樂。當知煩惱斷者，有如是等眾多勝利。復次，煩惱緣境略有十五。一、具分緣。謂身見等。二、一分緣。謂貪、瞋、慢等。三、有事緣。謂諸有事煩惱。四、無事緣。謂諸無事煩惱。
items.en: There is also one who cultivates conduct that benefits others, wishing to bring benefit and ease to sentient beings, having compassion for the world, causing gods and humans to attain benefit and ease. It should be known that severing affliction has such benefits as these, and many more. Moreover, the objects affliction references are, in brief, fifteen. First, comprehensive referencing, belonging to self-view and the rest. Second, partial referencing, belonging to greed, hatred, conceit, and the rest. Third, referencing a real object, belonging to those afflictions that have a real object. Fourth, referencing an unreal object, belonging to those afflictions that have no real object.

items.title: Section: Inner and Outer, Present and Absent, One's Own Kind and Another's

items.zh: 五、內緣。謂緣六處定不定地所有煩惱。六、外緣。謂緣妙五欲所有煩惱。七、現見緣。謂緣現在所有煩惱。八、不現見緣。謂緣去來所有煩惱。九、自類緣。謂緣自類煩惱所有煩惱。十、他類緣。謂緣異類煩惱及緣煩惱事所有煩惱。十一、有緣。謂緣後有所有煩惱。十二、無有緣。謂緣斷無有所有煩惱。
items.en: Fifth, inner referencing, belonging to affliction, whether in meditative absorption or not, that references the six sense-bases. Sixth, outer referencing, belonging to affliction that references the exquisite five sensory pleasures. Seventh, present referencing, belonging to affliction that references what is currently present. Eighth, absent referencing, belonging to affliction that references what is past or future. Ninth, referencing one's own kind, belonging to affliction that references affliction of its own kind. Tenth, referencing another kind, belonging to affliction that references affliction of a different kind, and the matters bound up with that affliction. Eleventh, existence-referencing, belonging to affliction that references future existence. Twelfth, non-existence-referencing, belonging to affliction that references the cutting off of existence.

items.title: Section: Twenty Kinds of Person Behind Every Manifestation of Affliction

items.zh: 十三、自境緣。謂欲界於欲行煩惱，色界於色行煩惱，無色界於無色行煩惱。十四、他境緣。謂色界於欲行煩惱，無色界於色行煩惱。又復下地於上地煩惱。所以者何？生上地者，於彼下地諸有情所，由常、恒、樂、淨具勝功德，自謂為勝故。十五、無境緣。謂緣分別所計滅道及廣大佛法等所有煩惱。復次，煩惱現行有二十種。謂二十種補特伽羅，依二十緣，起二十種現行煩惱。云何二十補特伽羅？一、在家，二、出家，三、住惡說法，四、住善說法，五、增上煩惱行，六、等分行，七、薄塵行，八、世間離欲，九、未離欲，十、見聖迹，十一、未見聖迹，十二、執著，十三、不執著，十四、觀察，十五、睡眠，十六、覺悟，十七、幼少，十八、根成熟，十九、般涅槃法，二十、不般涅槃法。
items.en: Thirteenth, referencing one's own realm, belonging to the desire realm's affliction towards desire-realm formations, the form realm's towards form-realm formations, and the formless realm's towards formless-realm formations. Fourteenth, referencing another realm, belonging to the form realm's affliction towards the desire realm, and the formless realm's towards the form realm; also, a lower realm's affliction towards a higher realm. Fifteenth, referencing no real object, belonging to affliction referencing what is merely computed through discrimination regarding cessation and the path, and the vast Dharma of the Buddha. Moreover, the active manifestation of affliction is of twenty kinds, referring to twenty kinds of person who, according to twenty conditions, generate twenty kinds of manifest affliction. What are the twenty kinds of person? First, the householder. Second, the renunciant. Third, one abiding in wrongly taught doctrine. Fourth, one abiding in correctly taught doctrine. Fifth, one of dominant affliction conduct. Sixth, one of evenly balanced conduct. Seventh, one of thin conduct. Eighth, one worldly free of desire. Ninth, one not yet free of desire. Tenth, one who has seen the noble footprint. Eleventh, one who has not yet seen it. Twelfth, one who clings. Thirteenth, one who does not cling. Fourteenth, one who examines. Fifteenth, one asleep. Sixteenth, one awake. Seventeenth, one young. Eighteenth, one of matured faculties. Nineteenth, one with the dharma of final nirvana. Twentieth, one without the dharma of final nirvana.

items.title: Section: Twenty Ways Affliction Actually Shows Its Face

items.zh: 云何二十煩惱現行？一、隨所欲纏現行，二、不隨所欲纏現行，三、無所了知煩惱現行，四、有所了知煩惱現行，五、麁煩惱現行，六、等煩惱現行，七、微煩惱現行，八、內門煩惱現行，九、外門煩惱現行，十、失念煩惱現行，十一、猛利煩惱現行，十二、分別所起煩惱現行，十三、任運所起煩惱現行，十四、尋思煩惱現行，十五、不自在煩惱現行，十六、自在煩惱現行，十七、非所依位煩惱現行，十八、所依位煩惱現行，十九、可救療煩惱現行，二十、不可救療煩惱現行。
items.en: What are the twenty kinds of manifest affliction? First, manifestation following one's own wish. Second, manifestation not following one's own wish. Third, manifestation without understanding. Fourth, manifestation with understanding. Fifth, coarse manifestation. Sixth, balanced manifestation. Seventh, subtle manifestation. Eighth, inner-door manifestation. Ninth, outer-door manifestation. Tenth, lost-mindfulness manifestation. Eleventh, forceful manifestation. Twelfth, discrimination-arisen manifestation. Thirteenth, spontaneous manifestation. Fourteenth, discursive manifestation. Fifteenth, uncontrolled manifestation. Sixteenth, freely willed manifestation. Seventeenth, manifestation prior to its proper basis. Eighteenth, manifestation at its proper basis. Nineteenth, curable manifestation. Twentieth, incurable manifestation.

items.zh: 云何二十煩惱現行緣？一、樂緣，二、苦緣，三、不苦不樂緣，四、欲緣，五、尋思緣，六、觸緣，七、隨眠緣，八、宿習緣，九、親近惡友緣，十、聞不正法緣，十一、不正作意緣，十二、不信緣，十三、懈怠緣，十四、失念緣，十五、散亂緣，十六、惡慧緣，十七、放逸緣，十八、煩惱緣，十九、未離欲緣，二十、異生性緣。

blocks.text: How can you tell affliction is gone? The treatise gives a picture of the freed person, and then catalogues the many faces of affliction.

Master Cháng Bǎi: though one deliberately brings the loveliest object to mind and examines it, no stain arises; the mind neither rejoices nor grieves. Though possessing all these virtues, the noble ones do not want others to know.
Master Cháng Bǎi: learners, severing part, attain coolness; arhats attain the foremost coolness. From the first fruit one passes beyond the lower realms.
Master Cháng Bǎi: beyond one's own good, one also accomplishes beings' good. Some afflictions take everything as object, some only part, some arise from inner discrimination alone.
Master Cháng Bǎi: afflictions arise on the six inner bases and the five outer sense pleasures, and also through craving for non-existence.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the "balanced" person has about equal greed, hatred, and delusion. Some afflictions concern even the Mahāyāna, as held by a discriminating mind.

Master Cháng Bǎi: householders love sense pleasure and affliction follows their wish; renunciants must curb desire, and until they succeed, affliction does not follow their wish. (Untranslated, 0629c02: twenty conditions for affliction to arise, from pleasure, pain, and desire to bad friends, wrong teaching, laziness, distraction, and ordinary-being status itself.)
"They do not want others to know." Real freedom does not advertise itself.

quiz.q: What is the mark regarding the agreeable once affliction is severed, and on seeing form?
options: even forceful attention to the loveliest brings no stain; no joy or sorrow, abiding in supreme equanimity, mindful
one no longer sees lovely things, the eye ceasing to work
great joy at seeing form
disgust at seeing form
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though one deliberately brings the loveliest object to mind and examines it, no stain arises; the mind neither rejoices nor sorrows, and always abides in supreme equanimity without clinging. This is the test for whether affliction is truly gone.

quiz.q: The English has "the very first" for 第一. What is wrong?
options: nothing: 第一 means the first time one tastes security, as the lecture says of learners, "foremost" being unnecessary
第一 is supreme, not first in time; learners gain security first, and only adepts' is foremost
"security" should be "insurance"
"coolness" should be "cold"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: arhats attain complete nirvāṇa and the foremost security; learners, severing part, attain coolness, and arhats the foremost coolness; what is realised at the learner stage is called only security and coolness. So "very first" reverses the sequence; "foremost" or "supreme" is needed.

quiz.q: At which stage does one pass evil destinies and all suffering of birth, and can present bliss regress?
options: from the first fruit past evil destinies, adepts past birth's; dull ones' bliss may regress, the path never
the first fruit passes all birth's suffering; bliss and the path never regress
only buddhas pass evil destinies
only gods pass evil destinies
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from the learner's first fruit one passes the suffering of evil destinies; passing all birth's suffering is the adept arhat's attainment. The absorption of present bliss may regress for the dull, yet the noble path never does. The English "according to one's own wish" misattaches the phrase.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain noble ones' few desires and delight in the unelaborated?
options: they have no wish at all, not even to help, and sit silently, refusing even to teach when asked
they like lively ceremonies
having virtues without wishing others to know; their mind is naturally pure, abiding in emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness
they like debate
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though possessing all these virtues, they do not want others to know; the noble mind is naturally pure, abiding in emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, and non-elaboration. They can still engage elaboration with effort, as the treatise says.

quiz.q: The English has "every perception of sense-based resistance." What is left out?
options: nothing: it is one item, every kind of resistance
it omits 色想
it omits perception of diversity: these are two items, 種種性 having become "every"
it omits 超越
quiz.why: The standard formula for the formless attainments lists three: passing perception of form, ending perception of resistance, and not attending to perception of diversity. The lecture likewise treats them separately. "Every perception of resistance" absorbs the third into the second, so perception of diversity is gone.

quiz.q: What does "one who cultivates conduct that benefits others" add?
options: only benefit to others, bodhisattvas giving up liberation, the passage setting hearers and bodhisattvas in opposition
beyond own benefit, benefiting beings; both are completed
powers
long life
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beyond one's own good, one also accomplishes beings' good, and self-benefit and benefit to others are both complete. §22 ended with own good fulfilled, and this sentence extends it. The English is close.

quiz.q: What are the first four of the fifteen objects?
options: inner, outer, present, absent
comprehensive, partial, real-object, no-object
own kind, other kind, existence, non-existence
own realm, other realm, none, comprehensive
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: taking all matters as object is comprehensive, as with self-view; partial takes a part, not all; the no-object afflictions arise from inner discrimination, with no real matter there. This repeats fascicle 58's distinction.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain inner and outer, existence and non-existence referencing?
options: inner is thought and outer sight; existence is belief in God and non-existence disbelief, unrelated to future lives
inner takes six bases, outer the five pleasures; existence takes next life, non-existence wishes it cut off
inner is one's home
existence means wealth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: those with or without absorption have afflictions on the six inner bases; outward they take the fine five sense pleasures; through craving for non-existence, afflictions wish to end future existence forever. Even the wish for annihilation is thus an affliction.

quiz.q: What does no-object referencing take, and what example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: all worldly things, objects not existing, greed for wealth being the example
computed cessation, path, and vast Dharma; as those wrongly grasping emptiness deny everything
affliction in sleep; dreams
higher afflictions; absorption
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this means afflictions on cessation, the path, and the vast inconceivable Mahāyāna as held by discriminating mind; or those who wrongly grasp emptiness, take up Madhyamaka, say nothing exists, and deny everything. Taking the Dharma as object is no guarantee of purity.

quiz.q: What are the "balanced" and "clinging" persons, and what do they depend on?
options: half greed and half hatred; hoarders, by twenty professions and no twenty conditions, unrelated to self
meditators; precept-keepers
those whose afflictions are about equal; those clinging to self; twenty conditions give rise to twenty manifestations
arhats; bodhisattvas
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the balanced person has about equal greed, hatred, and delusion; through discriminating, clinging to self and mine, taking all as real, greed, hatred, and delusion arise; this is clinging. The twenty conditions themselves are missing from the English, so §27's "these conditions" has no referent.

quiz.q: To whom belong manifestation following and not following one's wish, and lost-mindfulness manifestation?
options: laypeople follow; renunciants struggling do not; lost mindfulness is of noble ones too
renunciants follow, free of family; laypeople do not
all to ordinary beings
all to higher realms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: householders love sense pleasure and affliction follows their wish; renunciants must curb desire, and before succeeding have manifestation not following their wish; even those who have seen the noble tracks at times lose mindfulness. The twenty persons and twenty manifestations match in order.

quiz.q: The English has "controlled manifestation." Why is that a problem?
options: no problem: 自在 is self-control over affliction, 不自在 lacking it, both unrelated to sleep or waking, as the English shows
自在 means arising freely at will; "controlled" suggests being restrained, nearly the reverse
it should be "divine"
it should be "external"
quiz.why: The twenty persons and twenty manifestations are matched in order, so uncontrolled goes with one asleep, and 自在 with one awake, who can be greedy or angry at will. So 自在 describes affliction's free play. "Controlled" suggests the reverse. Master Cháng Bǎi's matching of the thirteenth shows the same principle.
